subject: Reserved GPU pool sizing & commercial options — DataWave production loadtests
messages:
From: Emma Lo <emma@datawave.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-15T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Prod sizing question — target throughput and commitment

Hi Soojin,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. To recap our needs for the upcoming production rollout: we expect a steady-state of ~200 inference requests/sec (payloads avg 600 tokens) with p95 latency goal <= 180ms, and traffic spikes up to ~600 req/s for short windows (5–10 minutes). We want a reserved GPU pool to guarantee throughput and predictable costs.

Can you confirm:
- What pool size (GPU count/type) you'd recommend to hit those numbers with ~10% headroom?
- Typical committed-month pricing for that pool and discount tiers for 12/24-months?
- Any performance-based credits if SLOs aren't met?

We can share our loadtest artifacts if helpful. Goal is to have a committed proposal to our procurement by 11/24.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Lo
Platform Lead, DataWave Inc
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lo <emma@datawave.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-16T11:04:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prod sizing question — target throughput and commitment

Emma — great to connect. Short answers up front and then we can follow up with a sizing test:

- Based on similar customers, initial estimate is 6–8 x A100 (or equivalent A800/Q4) dedicated GPUs to meet sustained 200 req/s (600 tokens avg) with p95 around 140–160ms and ~20% headroom for batching. For the 600 req/s spikes, we'd put autoscaling/burst capacity or a larger reserved buffer (10–12 GPUs) depending on how long spikes last.

- Pricing: we typically show three reserved-commit tiers:
  * Pilot (3 months) — small committed capacity, minimal discount
  * Production (12 months) — typical discount 15–20% vs on-demand, explicit throughput SLA
  * Enterprise (24+ months) — up to 25% discount + dedicated support

- Performance credits: we can build a service-credit clause tied to p95 latency misses during normal traffic windows; for spikes caused by customer traffic bursts we propose a separate investigation window.

Can you send the raw loadtest (traces + tps csv) and any dashboards — we’ll run them through our benchmark harness and get an objective sizing + cost estimate. Looping in Laura (solutions) to coordinate the test and Dev (infra) for the runbook.

Best,
Soojin
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: Emma Lo <emma@datawave.com>
Date: 2026-11-17T08:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prod sizing question — initial bench run results attached

Hi all,

We ran DataWave's baseline loadtest on our internal benchmark harness (attached traces + tps csv). Quick summary of the 2026-11-17 test (configs in attachments):

Environment: 8 x A100 (80GB) dedicated pool, continuous batching, KV cache enabled
Observed:
- Sustained 200 req/s (600 tokens avg): p50=62ms, p95=148ms, p99=220ms
- Short 6-minute spike to 600 req/s (replay): median latency rose to ~210ms, p95 ~380ms during peak, recovery within 90s
- Max sustainable steady-state before p95 blowup: ~260 req/s on this pool size
- Token throughput: ~1.2M tokens/s aggregate across the pool at peak

Notes:
- With quantized model variant (INT8) we see ~25% higher tokens/s and slightly higher p95 variance — tradeoff between cost and latency stability.
- Adding a 2-GPU burst buffer reduced peak p95 by ~35% in replayed spikes.

Attachments: datawave_tps_summary_20261117.csv, loadtest_traces_20261117.zip, dashboard_snapshot_20261117.png

If DataWave wants firm throughput guarantees for 600 req/s spikes, recommendation is 10–12 GPUs reserved or 8 GPUs reserved + 4-GPU burst pool. Pricing impact below in the sales thread.

—Dev
Staff SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Emma Lo <emma@datawave.com>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: Patrick Nguyen <patrick@datawave.com>, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-18T09:46:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prod sizing question — initial bench run results attached

Thanks Dev — this is super helpful. A few clarifying Qs:
1) If we pick 8 GPUs reserved (your mid-point), what monthly committed spend range should we expect (ballpark) for 12-month vs 24-month?
2) For the quantized variant: can we guarantee functional parity for our prompts? We rely on some subtle scoring in-system.
3) Can we include a performance-credit structure tied to p95 for sustained hours (not during large replayed spikes)?

Procurement wants a clear delta between 12 vs 24 month economics and an example SLA clause. Also curious if Redwood will entertain a higher up-front commit in exchange for a steeper discount (we're looking at a 36% total TCO reduction target vs current cloud GPU ops).

—Emma
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lo <emma@datawave.com>, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-19T10:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prod sizing question — commercial proposal (8 GPU baseline)

Emma — thanks for the patience. Based on Dev's bench and Soojin's sizing guidance, here is a commercial starter proposal for an 8-GPU reserved pool (A100-class):

Option A — 12-month reserved (Production):
- Committed monthly spend: $48,000
- Effective discount vs on-demand: 18%
- Included burst buffer: 1 GPU (pay-as-you-use beyond commit)
- SLA: p95 latency <= 180ms for sustained traffic windows (non-abusive spikes excluded). Missed SLO: 5% service credit per calendar week, capped at 20% per quarter.

Option B — 24-month reserved (Enterprise):
- Committed monthly spend: $41,000
- Effective discount: 25%
- Included burst buffer: 2 GPUs
- Additional: quarterly architecture review + dedicated solutions hours (8 hrs/quarter)

Concession ask: For a 36% TCO reduction target we discussed, we can offer a blended approach — 24-month commit plus upfront purchase of 2 extra GPUs for longer-term amortization and an additional one-time onboarding credit of 2 months of service if committed within two weeks.

Performance-credit ask from your side is reasonable; we propose the service-credit language above and we can refine the SLO windows (e.g., exclude traffic spikes >3x baseline or if customer-side rate-limiter misconfiguration is detected).

Next steps:
- If this aligns, we’ll prepare a formal term sheet and a DocuSign for signatures.
- Recommend a 2-week PoC/canary run on the 8-GPU pool with your real traffic + our tracing enabled — we’ll use that to baseline the final SLA clause.

—Aditya
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Emma Lo <emma@datawave.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, soojin_lee@redwood.ai
Cc: patrick@datawave.com
Date: 2026-11-19T14:55:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prod sizing question — commercial proposal (8 GPU baseline)

Aditya / Soojin — appreciate the detailed proposal. A few items from procurement and platform:
- The 24-month price looks in the right direction but procurement is pushing for a deeper discount in exchange for immediate 3-month upfront payment. Is there room to move another 3–5% on the 24-month band for that?
- We want a stronger performance-credit mechanism for sustained p95 misses (example: 10% credit for any calendar week where p95 > 180ms for more than 4 hours cumulative). Is Redwood able to accept that level or only the lower cap you proposed?
- For quantized model parity: we’ll run our eval prompts in the PoC, but any regression mechanism (alerts + rollback) should be included in the canary plan.

If you can confirm adjustments we’ll fast-track the legal and procurement loop.

Thanks,
Emma
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Lo <emma@datawave.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-11-20T15:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Prod sizing question — commercial proposal (8 GPU baseline)

Emma — thanks. Internal takeaways and a path forward:

1) Commercial flexibility: we can offer an additional 3% on the 24-month band for a 3-month upfront payment (so target 28% total discount). Finance needs to sign off on final numbers but this is in the acceptable range.

2) Performance credits: we can accept the stronger weekly-style performance credit language you requested with a 10% credit for weeks where p95 > 180ms for more than 4 cumulative hours, with one week waiver allowed for initial onboarding. We will also exclude misconfigured client-side bursts (we’ll provide rate-limiter detector logs as evidence).

3) Quantized parity & rollback: agreed — the PoC will include your eval prompt set and an automated rollback trigger if quality regressions exceed agreed thresholds. Laura will own the canary runbook and will schedule the PoC next Monday.

Next steps: Laura, could you set the PoC calendar invite and include the test plan (we’ll attach our trace collector and expected metrics)? Aditya, once PoC is scheduled, please circulate a term sheet draft and the DocuSign link. Emma, we’ll aim to have a formal proposal in your procurement queue by 11/24.

Best,
Soojin
